how_i_worked.clips: Decoded with toolchain/ffmpeg/ffmpeg piping rawvideo rgb24 to numpy, one frame at a time, holding only the previous frame. No PNG or any other file was written into the repository. Frame counts confirmed with toolchain/ffmpeg/ffprobe -count_frames: 06=286, 07=421, 08=735, 11=300, 15=448, all 1080x2340 at 62.5 fps, matching frames.json.
how_i_worked.luma: Rec.601 on the full-resolution RGB: 0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B, kept as float. Where a report's number only reproduced under a different convention (PIL's 8-bit L, or <= rather than <) I say so in the correction rather than silently adopting it.
how_i_worked.held_frame_test: The brief's own three terms, all of which must hold against the previous frame: mean absolute change < 0.5 grey levels, share of pixels changing by more than two < 0.0015, busiest 32-px tile mean change < 2.0. Run at full resolution on every frame of all five clips.
how_i_worked.paper_mask: (luma > 150) & ((R - B) < 40), the mask the material-truth report states, so its numbers and mine are comparable. Edges were walked per column from a seed row inside the piece rather than taken as the extreme paper row in a band, because a band catches the next sheet down.
how_i_worked.code: Read-only: grep and sed -n over app/. I did NOT run the test suite. The completeness pass of cycle 10 found that running it rewrote two files in evidence/; I checked the fix instead of re-triggering the fault (see disclosure).

Band x40-1040, y1250-1520 of frame 734 reads max luma 184, 99th percentile 111, share above 190 of 0.00000, while the text line 50 px above has 4.69 per cent above 150. The row opens 178 device px at frame 688 and stays empty through 734.
corrections.what_i_measured: Survives, and I can state it harder than the report does. Reading the app's own rows_cost in evidence/logs/08_state_propagating.report.json - row 8078, type 'message', tall 72, top 337 of viewport_tall 501.4 - and fixing the viewport origin from row 8079's declared top of 409 against the legal pad's measured paper top at device y1544 (scale 3, scenes/08 dpr 3), row 8078 occupies device y1328-1544. In frame 734 that 216-px band carries 0.213 per cent of its pixels above luma 190 and 0.591 per cent above 150; the legal-pad row immediately below it carries 46.6 and 49.4 per cent. A 219-fold difference: the row is blank. The report's own band reads max 182.5 (claim 184), p99 109.7 (claim 111), share above 190 exactly 0.00000 (claim 0.00000); the line above reads 4.67 per cent above 150 over y1200-1250 (claim 4.69). The app also lists the id in `visible`, in `whole_on_the_glass`, in `paper` with stock lined_02 and tear tear_029, and reports paper_whole_on_the_glass 2 when only one paper note draws. Held run 690-734 confirmed at 45 frames. One number does NOT reproduce: the gap from the 'noor is quiet' line to the legal pad goes 367 -> 277 device px in my measurement (shrinking), not 99 -> 277; what grows is the space ABOVE that line, 21 -> 234 px, and the total empty band between the two paper pieces goes 427 -> 548 px.
corrections.does_it_survive: yes - the load-bearing measurement is confirmed and strengthened; one supporting figure (99 -> 277) is wrong in direction and should be replaced with the rows_cost derivation above

It should not be left resting on a landmark distance that a re-measurement inverts, when the app's own layout record makes the same point exactly: the app says 72 CSS px of message is whole on the glass and drawn on paper, and 216 device px of that band are bare desk.

corrections.claim: Inside the big note on 02_chat.png, 67 ink components of 120 px or more match each other at native scale with a median best-match IoU of 0.766, p90 0.936, max 0.957, and 23 of 67 (34 per cent) have a twin at IoU >= 0.85; stroke half-width is mean 2.01 px with CV 0.225 and correlates with ink luma at only -0.130.

not_looked_at.note_on_that_list: Coverage this cycle is the best thing about the review's bookkeeping. The union of the six `opened` lists reaches 122 of the 123 core files in evidence/ - everything except one per-clip frames log - and the single omission is a duplicate of an entry in frames.json that three reports read. Per-critic: anti_goal 77, coherence 75, messenger_reliability 69, material_truth 47, emotional_transmission 45, code 5 (its evidence is app/, listed separately and correctly). Two real thinnesses remain. The first is evidence/.previous/: every artifact in the set carries a label measured against it and only one critic opened it, so five rows were scored on a set whose 'improved / regressed' basis they never saw. I checked the baseline myself so nobody has to take it on trust - all fifteen previous_sha values in DIFF.json match the sha256 prefix of the file sitting in evidence/.previous/, and all fifteen current sha values match the artifact on disk, so the baseline is real and the briefing's claim about it is true. verdict: This is a review somebody could act on, and it is a markedly better one than its own vocabulary problem last cycle: all six rows are now internally coherent. Each of the three rows below its floor - messenger reliability at 22 of 26, material truth at 21 of 22, emotional transmission at 16 of 17 - names exactly one blocking finding and says in its verdict which one is holding it there, and the two rows that meet their floors carry none, which is what the briefing asked for and did not get last time. The row 01 disqualifier is also scored the way the brief requires, strictly below the floor rather than at it. The measurements are mostly real. I re-ran every blocking finding and every serious one with my own code and the great majority reproduce, several to the digit: the 113,175-pixel slab on 01_pulse to the pixel, its bounding box, its mean and its maximum; the corner triangle's bounding box, its median colour #CFC8B8, its 0.26 grey levels of tooth and - the test the whole finding turns on - a mean AND maximum absolute difference of exactly 0.0 between day and dusk over its interior while the desk ninety pixels away moves 25.7; the scroll's 82 frames of 724 over 16 ms and 26 over 33; the 435 glyph pixels of the search chip; the 34-against-36 hole in surfaces.json; three of the code row's four serious findings at the lines they cite. The strongest finding in the cycle got stronger under re-measurement: the app's own rows_cost declares row 8078 a 72-CSS-pixel message, whole on the glass, drawn on lined_02 with tear_029, and the 216 device pixels it occupies in frame 734 carry 0.213 per cent of their pixels above paper brightness against 46.6 per cent for the note below it. Six things need correcting and two of them change what a reader should do. MANIFEST.json strikes 07_feeling_landing.mp4 and 15_authored_feeling.mp4 from the capture on held-frame counts of 154 and 129; the brief's own three-term test gives 0 and 40, their own frames logs give 0 and 40, and two critics and now I have measured it. The builder's self-score for emotional transmission - 15, the lower of the two and therefore the score the row carries - rests its entire written justification on those two numbers. Beyond that: the messenger row's blocking finding is right but its supporting gap figure inverts on re-measurement and should be replaced by the rows_cost derivation; the material row's blocking finding is right but its '+250 px' figure and its '98.6 per cent / 100 per cent' shares do not hold at 87.8 and 90 / 85; the emotional row's account of the reception pick-up as 'a fresh profile that has never paired' is refuted by store 'kept' and events 14062 in the two records beneath it, which makes the fault worse rather than better; material truth's assertion that 'nothing in the set is a stale still' is contradicted by the MANIFEST it cites, which counts twelve artifacts of seventeen; and the two reports describing the same dark wedge on 01_pulse differ by 14,000 pixels because one of them rounded to eight bits without saying so. One serious code finding - the per-type switch in _ReplyStrip - cannot be checked at all any more: there is no switch anywhere in app/lib, _ReplyStrip calls summaryOf, and the file carries a comment describing the reported bug in the past tense, because note.dart was rewritten twenty-eight minutes after the report was filed. That last point is the gap that matters most and it is invisible from inside every rubric row. Twelve source and test paths were rewritten between 19:58 and 20:07, after the final critic report at 19:49, and seven files including evidence/scenes/08_state_propagating.json are dirty in a tree that was clean when I started. The artifacts, logs and crops are untouched, so the picture half of this review will still be there tomorrow; the source half and the framing half will not. Coverage is otherwise good - the union of the six opened lists reaches 122 of 123 core files, missing only one duplicate per-clip frames log - though five of six rows were scored without anyone opening evidence/.previous/, whose fifteen hashes I checked against DIFF.json myself so that nobody has to take the baseline on trust. Taking the lower of critic and builder per row gives 22 + 21 + 15 + 13 + 9 = 80, three floors unmet and four artifacts labelled regressed, so the cheapest real move in this cycle is not a new capture: it is correcting two numbers in MANIFEST, which would return two clips to the set without shooting anything.
